Dated this the 09th day of January, 2025  ORDER
This Bail Application is filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No. 848 of 2024 of Kumarakom Police Station, Kottayam registered alleging offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(h) of IPC, and Section 4 r/w 3,6 r/w 5(l)(II) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution case is that, in May 2024, the accused reached the house of the victim aged 17 years, who was residing in Thiruvarppu Panchayath in Kottayam, and promised the victim that the petitioner would marry her, and committed rape on the victim with penetrative intercourse.
Later when the victim was taken to hospital with the complaint of stomach pain, the Doctor suggested scanning.
During scanning, her pregnancy was BAIL APPL. NO. 11260 OF 2024 2025:KER:1259 detected and Scan Centre reported the crime.
The Petitioner was arrested on 03.10.2024, and he is in custody.
4. The petitioner approached this Court with an earlier bail application as B.A.No. 9329 of 2024.
This Court was not inclined to grant bail, and this Court allowed to withdraw the bail application with the liberty to move the trial court after some time.
The petitioner moved the Sessions Court again, and the learned Sessions Judge again dismissed the bail application.
Hence this second Bail application is filed.
5. Heard counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
6. It is true that the allegation against the petitioner is very serious.
But the fact remains that the petitioner has been in custody since 03.10.2024, which is more than 97 days.
The petitioner is aged 22 years.
According to the petitioner, he was in a love affair with the victim.
Considering the fact that the petitioner is in custody from 03.10.2024, and he is in custody for about 97 days, this Bail Application is allowed after imposing stringent conditions.

Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870], after considering all the earlier judgments,
observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

8. Moreover, in Jalaluddin Khan v. Union of India [2024 KHC 6431], the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that:
"21.

entities.text: Jalaluddin Khan v. Union of India [2024 KHC 6431]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before we part with the Judgment, we must mention here that the Special Court and the High Court did not consider the material in the charge sheet objectively.
Perhaps the focus was more on the activities of PFI, and therefore, the appellant's case could not be properly appreciated.

When a case is made out for a grant of bail,
the Courts should not have any hesitation in granting bail.
The allegations of the prosecution may be very serious.
But, the duty of the Courts is to consider the case for grant of bail in accordance with the law.
"Bail is the rule and jail is an exception" is a settled law.

Even in a case like the present case where there are stringent BAIL APPL.
NO. 11260 OF 2024 2025:KER:1259 conditions for the grant of bail in the relevant statutes, the same rule holds good with only modification that the bail can be granted if the conditions in the statute are satisfied.
The rule also means that once a case is made out for the grant of bail, the Court cannot decline to grant bail.
If the Courts start denying bail in deserving cases, it will be a violation of the rights guaranteed under Art.21 of our Constitution."
(underline supplied)

9. In Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement [2024 KHC 6426], also the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that:
"53.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement [2024 KHC 6426]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court further observed that, over a period of time, the trial courts and the High Courts have forgotten a very well - settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment.
From our experience, we can say that it appears that the trial courts and the High Courts attempt to play safe in matters of grant of bail.
The principle that bail is a rule and refusal is an exception is, at times, followed in breach.

On account of non - grant of bail even in straight forward open and shut cases, this Court is flooded with huge number of bail petitions thereby BAIL APPL. NO. 11260 OF 2024 2025:KER:1259 adding to the huge pendency.
It is high time that the trial courts and the High Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is rule and jail is exception"."
10. Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this cae, this bail application is allowed with the following directions.

1. Petitioner shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.

The petitioner shall co-operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
3. Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.
4. Petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the BAIL APPL. NO. 11260 OF 2024 2025:KER:1259 offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
5. If any of the above conditions are violated by the petitioner, the jurisdictional Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though the bail is granted by this Court.
The prosecution and the victim are at liberty to approach the jurisdictional court to cancel the bail, if there is any violation of the above conditions.

I make it clear that the petitioner shall not enter into the jurisdictional limits of Kumarakom police station except for the purpose of appearing before the Investigating Officer and jurisdictional court.
